name: Miso Glazed Salmon with Stir-Fried Vegetables

components.name: Miso-Glazed Salmon
steps: Mix 120 g white miso, 80 ml mirin, 60 ml soy, 15 g ginger paste, 20 g brown sugar and white pepper. Coat salmon and chill for 30 minutes.
Wipe excess wet glaze from salmon. Heat remaining peanut oil in a heavy skillet and place salmon skin-side down.
Sear until nicely coloured, turn gently and finish to a safe core temperature of 63 C for make-ahead service.
Bring any marinade that contacted raw fish to a full boil before reducing it to a glaze; alternatively reserve a clean portion before marinating.
Portion five servings of salmon and vegetables; chill quickly and use early-week or freeze later-week containers.

components.name: Stir-Fried Vegetables
steps: Warm 15 ml peanut oil in a wok, stir-fry trimmed broccoli, beans and carrots for 5-7 minutes. Finish with sesame oil, sesame seeds and measured salt; transfer out.

Jack publishes 464 kcal, 45.8 g protein, 31 g carbs, 19 g fat per portion. UNHANGRY fixes unspecified weights for salmon and vegetables, so nutrition is recalculated and is NOT Jack's published result.
Storing & reheating: Source recommends 3 days refrigerated or 2 months frozen. Freeze as soon as cool if intended for later week. For safety, cook to 63 C and reheat thoroughly.
Allergens: Fish, Soy or soy-containing sauce, Sesame, May contain alcohol

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
